overview: Nomura Holdings is Japan's largest securities brokerage and investment bank, headquartered in Tokyo and listed on the NYSE via ADRs (1 ADR = 1 ordinary share, SEC foreign private issuer filing 20-F/6-K). The group operates through three segments — Wealth Management, Investment Management, and Wholesale (global markets and investment banking) — serving retail and institutional clients, corporates, financial institutions, and governments. Nomura has a dominant domestic Japanese franchise alongside a global wholesale and asset-management footprint across the Americas, EMEA, and Asia ex-Japan, with roughly half of consolidated net revenue still generated in Japan.

business_model.summary: Nomura is a diversified securities group blending a stable, fee-based domestic retail wealth/asset-management business with a market-sensitive global wholesale (trading, underwriting, M&A advisory) business. Wealth Management and Investment Management generate more recurring, asset-based revenue (AUM fees, recurring advisory fees), while Wholesale revenue is transaction- and market-driven (fixed income, equities trading, underwriting, advisory fees) and more volatile quarter to quarter.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2C (Japanese retail wealth clients) and B2B/institutional (corporates, financial institutions, governments, asset owners)
business_model.geographic_mix: Japan ~48-53%, Americas ~28-34%, EMEA ~15-16%, Asia/Oceania ~2-3% of net revenue (based on recent quarterly disclosures); management is pushing for a higher non-Japan mix following the Macquarie asset management acquisition, which brings AUM managed outside Japan above 35%

competitive_position.market_position: Clear leader in Japanese equity research/advisory and trading share domestically (historically 12-16% share of institutional Japanese equity trading, ahead of Daiwa and Mizuho); globally a mid-tier wholesale player versus US bulge-bracket banks, but the largest Asia-headquartered global investment bank with meaningful Americas and EMEA wholesale operations

moat_factors.description: Largest retail brokerage network and relationship base in Japan, giving unmatched reach for wealth management and underwriting distribution
100+ year history and brand recognition as Japan's flagship securities house, though dented periodically by compliance scandals
One of few Asian banks with genuine Americas/EMEA fixed income, equities and M&A advisory capability (bolstered by Nomura Greentech, Instinet, Lehman's non-US franchise acquired in 2008)

moat_factors.factor: Scale in asset management post-Macquarie deal
moat_factors.description: Macquarie US/European public asset management acquisition (~$1.8bn, closed Dec 2025) lifts Investment Management AUM to ~$770bn, improving scale economics and non-Japan diversification
Extensive global broker-dealer and banking licenses across Japan, US, UK and other jurisdictions are costly and slow for new entrants to replicate

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on volatile, market-sensitive Wholesale trading and underwriting revenue versus more fee-stable US/European peers
Sub-scale relative to US bulge-bracket banks (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley) in global investment banking league tables and capital base
History of internal control and compliance lapses (bond market spoofing scandal, insider information leaks) that periodically damage client trust and invite regulatory scrutiny
Structurally low profitability versus global peers; ROE only recently reached double digits after years of single-digit returns
Japan's slow-growth, low-rate domestic economy constrains underlying retail brokerage and banking revenue growth absent fee/AUM mix shift

growth_drivers: Management Vision 2030: roadmap to sustainably lift consolidated ROE to 10-12%+ and pre-tax income above ¥750bn (raised from original 8-10% ROE / ¥500bn target after both were effectively achieved early)
Macquarie US/European public asset management acquisition (closed Dec 2025, ~US$180bn AUM added) scaling Investment Management and lifting AUM outside Japan to over 35% of the franchise

Wealth Management recurring-revenue build-out: 17 consecutive quarters of positive net inflows, record recurring revenue, and new deposit-sweep product (launched April 2026) integrating banking with wealth management
Wholesale structural reform driving record pre-tax income across Equities and Fixed Income, with Equities revenue up 41% YoY and Fixed Income up 11% YoY in Q1 FY2027
Continued US/global wholesale expansion built on the Lehman Brothers Asia/Europe franchise and Nomura Greentech (sustainable technology/infrastructure M&A advisory)
Headquarters relocation expected to shift costs from rent to depreciation, with flat-to-declining total costs medium-term, supporting operating leverage
Japanese retail investor base growth from NISA (tax-free investment account) expansion driving inflows into brokerage and asset management products

business.description: Trading and underwriting revenue is highly sensitive to market conditions; management itself flagged that wholesale net revenue 'slowed somewhat' entering H2 FY2027 amid expected volatility from US midterm elections and monetary policy shifts

2024-2025 bond market spoofing/manipulation scandal (fired trader Takushi Sawada) led to FSA-recommended fines, executive pay clawbacks, and reputational damage; recurrence risk remains given history of past incidents

business.risk: Integration risk from Macquarie asset management acquisition
business.description: Combining a ~$180bn AUM acquired business with Nomura Asset Management carries execution, cultural, and client-retention risk, and goodwill impairment risk if synergies disappoint

business.risk: Competitive pressure from both domestic (Daiwa, SMBC Nikko, Mizuho, MUFG Morgan Stanley) and global bulge-bracket banks
business.description: Nomura must defend domestic leadership while competing with far larger global players in wholesale and investment banking

financial.description: Yen-denominated results translated to USD for ADR holders; JPY weakness or strength materially affects reported USD earnings and dividends independent of underlying JPY performance
Revenue and profitability are leveraged to global capital markets activity (issuance, M&A, trading volumes), which can decline sharply in risk-off environments

Subject to Basel III and multiple jurisdictions' capital/liquidity rules; CET1 ratio reported around 13.07% and total capital ratio ~16.10% as of late 2025, providing cushion, but future rule changes could raise capital costs

regulatory.risk: Japan FSA and multi-jurisdictional regulatory scrutiny
regulatory.description: Ongoing regulatory attention following the bond-market manipulation case; Nomura operates under overlapping Japanese, US, UK and other regulatory regimes with evolving rules (Basel III finalization, market conduct rules)

20-F risk factors cite exposure to litigation/claims tied to underwriting, securities offerings, and complex trading arrangements, which could be costly and reputationally damaging, especially in market downturns

macro.risk: Bank of Japan monetary policy shifts
macro.description: Rising Japanese rates affect bond trading, banking margins, and retail investor behavior (competing bank deposit yields vs. brokerage products)

macro.risk: US/global interest rate and election-driven volatility
macro.description: Management explicitly flagged anticipated H2 FY2027 volatility tied to US midterm elections and shifting monetary policy, which cuts both ways for a trading-heavy wholesale business
A slowdown in global capital markets activity, equity issuance, or M&A would directly compress Wholesale net revenue, the largest segment

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global investment banking and wealth management markets are recovering with increased capital markets issuance, trading volumes, and growing retail investor participation in Japan (aided by NISA reforms); Japanese asset management is consolidating as scale becomes more important
macro_factors.cyclicality: High in Wholesale (trading/underwriting/advisory revenue tracks capital markets cycles); moderate-to-low in Wealth Management and Investment Management given recurring AUM-based fees
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high; Bank of Japan policy normalization affects bond trading and banking margins, while global rate moves affect fixed income trading revenue and client risk appetite
key_input_costs: Compensation and headcount costs (largest expense line)

recent_developments.event: Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended June 2026) results: ROE of 15.4%, the highest since Q2 2020; record pre-tax income in Wealth Management, Investment Management and Wholesale divisions

Completed acquisition of Macquarie's US and European public asset management business for ~$1.8 billion, adding ~$180bn in AUM and lifting Nomura Asset Management's global AUM to ~$770bn (35%+ managed outside Japan)

FY2026 (fiscal year ended March 31, 2026) full-year results: net revenue of ¥2,167.7bn (+14.5% YoY), full-year ROE of 10.1%; Wealth Management net revenue +12.5% to ¥487.9bn, Wholesale net revenue +9.9% to ¥1,162.2bn, Investment Management net revenue +34.3% to ¥258.5bn; declared year-end dividend of ¥24/share (full-year dividend ¥51/share)
Completed share buyback program (resolution Jan 30, 2026); cumulative repurchases of ~46.86 million shares for ~¥60.0bn as of mid-April 2026
Launched deposit sweep service integrating banking and wealth management offerings

Fired bond trader Takushi Sawada publicly defended himself via anonymous blog following his 2024 dismissal over a Japanese government bond futures spoofing investigation; SESC recommended an FSA fine (~¥21.8m) on Nomura's domestic securities unit; CEO Kentaro Okuda had voluntarily returned 20% of pay for two months in response to the scandal
JPMorgan and BofA analysts upgraded Nomura to Buy, citing structural reform progress and improved profitability (average price target ~$10.20)

Management revised 2030 Vision targets upward to ROE of 10-12%+ (from 8-10%+) and pre-tax income of over ¥750bn (from over ¥500bn), reflecting the fact original targets were already being approached/exceeded

guidance.as_of: Q1 FY2027 Earnings (July 2026) / FY2026 Full-Year Results (April 2026)
guidance.fiscal_year: FY2027 (year ending March 31, 2027), medium-term to FY2030

items.notes: Raised from original 8-10%+ target after the company already achieved double-digit ROE (10.1% FY2026 full year; 15.4% in Q1 FY2027)
Raised from over ¥500bn original target; FY2026 segment pre-tax income already showed strong growth (Wealth Management +22.8%, Wholesale +20.6%)

items.target: No specific new buyback plan committed
items.notes: CFO emphasized balancing growth investment (including integration of Macquarie asset management deal) with shareholder returns; avoided committing to a new specific buyback program as of the Q1 FY2027 call
Reflects improved full-year profitability (ROE 10.1%); no explicit FY2027 dividend target disclosed yet

items.target: Flat to slightly declining total costs medium-term
items.notes: Headquarters relocation shifts rent expense to depreciation; management expects neutral-to-positive effect on overall expense base

guidance.management_commentary: CFO Moriuchi flagged that wholesale net revenue 'slowed somewhat of late' heading into H2 FY2027, partly seasonal, and that 'market volatility is likely to increase in the second half' due to US midterm elections and shifts in monetary policy. Management reiterated confidence in the raised 2030 Vision targets (ROE 10-12%+, pre-tax income >¥750bn) following record quarterly results across all three core segments, while stressing continued investment in growth (notably integrating the Macquarie asset management acquisition) alongside shareholder returns.

bull_case: Structural reform is visibly working: Q1 FY2027 ROE of 15.4% is the highest since 2020, with record pre-tax income across Wealth Management, Investment Management, and Wholesale simultaneously
Macquarie asset management acquisition materially scales Investment Management (AUM to ~$770bn) and diversifies revenue away from Japan, with over 35% of AUM now managed for clients outside Japan

Wealth Management has delivered 17 consecutive quarters of positive net inflows with record recurring revenue, showing a genuine shift toward stickier, fee-based income away from transactional brokerage
Raised 2030 Vision targets (ROE 10-12%+, pre-tax income >¥750bn) signal management confidence, and recent results are already tracking toward/exceeding the low end of these targets

Capital return program (buybacks completed, rising dividend to ¥51/share) alongside a reasonably well-capitalized balance sheet (CET1 ~13%) gives flexibility to return excess capital while still investing in growth
bear_case: Wholesale segment remains the largest and most volatile revenue driver; management itself warned of slowing wholesale revenue and rising volatility heading into H2 FY2027 tied to US elections and monetary policy shifts

History of compliance failures (2024-2025 bond market spoofing scandal, trader firing, FSA fine, executive pay clawbacks) raises questions about internal controls and could recur, denting reputation and inviting regulatory scrutiny

Despite recent improvement, Nomura's profitability has historically lagged global bulge-bracket peers (Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley) and even raised targets (10-12% ROE) remain below what top-tier global investment banks sustainably generate
Heavy reliance on the slow-growth Japanese economy and yen-denominated earnings exposes USD-based ADR holders to currency translation risk independent of underlying business performance
Integration risk from the recently closed, sizable Macquarie asset management acquisition (~$1.8bn) could disappoint if synergies, client retention, or cultural integration underperform expectations
